properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8196496
Permit API: 081-21357
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Lewis Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 8/05/2024
Comments: On August 5, 2024, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an incident inspection at the Range Resources Cornwall 1-5H Pad. Range Resources Kirby Steck reported to the spill hotline that a swage on one of the lines to one of the production fluid tanks had broke and released approximately 15 gallons of produced fluid outside of the secondary containment. Upon arrival onsite, Range contractors had already scraped up the impacted soil. The area that was scraped was approximately 20 ft. X 10 ft. and the top inch or two inches had been removed. A roll off dumpster is scheduled to arrive on site in the late morning.The spilling of production fluid outside of secondary containment onto the well pad surface is a violation of the Clean Streams Law 402(b), Chapter 78a.57(a), and Solid Waste Management Act 301. Since, the spill was immediately cleaned up, the violations are considered immediately corrected.

Violation ID: 926724
Permit API: 059-25352
Unconventional: Yes
County: Greene
Municipality: Center Twp
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 8/16/2021
Comments: The operator submitted a Notice of Intent and Alternate Method of Plugging to the Department for the Thunder Unit One 1V gas well. The Department reviewed the well record and related information and determined that the well was not drilled and cased in conformance with casing and cementing requirements in the 2012 Oil and Gas Act (58 Pa. C.S. §§ 3201-3274) and 25 Pa. Code Chapter 78. The operator failed to segregate and protect the workable Pittsburgh coal seam by setting and cementing a coal protective casing across the workable Pittsburgh coal seam. The operator failed to drill approximately 50 feet below the Deepest Fresh Groundwater (DFGW) and permanently cement a surface casing at that depth. DFGW was identified on the well record at 780 feet. 13 3/8" surface casing was set and cemented at 284 feet. Quarterly Mechanical Integrity Assessment data (MIA) and regulatory Inactive well annual mechanical integrity data was not submitted to the Department for the following inspection years. 2020, 2019, 2018, 2017, 2016, 2014, and 2013. The Thunder Unit One 1V was on inactive status from 9/10/2013-9/10/2018.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 8/02/2023 to DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC in Derry Township, Westmoreland county. 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/02/2023
Violation Code: 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
Violation ID: 8154408
Permit API: 129-27013
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Derry Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 8/02/2023
Comments: On August 2, 2023, the Department conducted an inspection in response to a spill report. The spill was called in to the Department today at 9:54 AM by the Operator, who described a 25-26 barrel release of crude oil that was found by a well tender at 8:40 AM. Operator will be utilizing Act 2 standards for clean up.The Department arrived on site at approximately 1:15 PM and spoke with Paul Steiner of Diversified. According to Steiner, a well tender discovered the release at approximately 8:40 AM from a crack (Photo 3) in the storage/production tank on site. Steiner approximated the total release to be 26 barrels based on the amount of crude oil in the production tank last week (approximately 4 feet) and the amount of crude oil still in the tank at discovery, which is an approximate 22 inches.The release migrated towards and past the production equipment (Photo 4) and down an embankment, where it reportedly stopped at a berm (Photo 8) according to Steiner. Steiner is using a PID meter to detect the extent of the oil's migration. During the on site inspection, Diversified was excavating impacted material at the berm and moving it upslope so that they can place it into a Spartan dump truck to have it transported for disposal. Steiner says one truck load will be transported tonight, excavation will stop, then another Spartan truck will arrive tomorrow morning, excavation will resume, and remaining impacted material will be taken off site before Moody arrives in the afternoon to confirm complete site clean up. Oil absorbent booms will be placed around and downslope of the impacted material overnight tonight to prevent further migration between truck loads, according to Steiner.Following the inspection, Steiner and myself spoke with DCNR Park Manager Kris Baker of Keystone State Park at the park office to notify the park of the release.Violations issued for spill. The Department requests disposal documents when made available.

Permit API: 085-24169
Unconventional: No
County: Mercer

Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/09/2022
Comments: Routine field inspection performed in late morning with cold, partly sunny weather conditions, and 40 degrees. Last inspection performed on 8/6/18, more than 4 years ago. Wellhead is located in soybean Agriculture field planted/harvested ~350' NNW of surface/ground production equipment (photo #1). The wellhead is in close, visible proximity to the production facility (photo #2). At the wellhead surface casing valve is open, lower right side production tubular valve cracked open to port with valve open to drip/domestic house gas meter run, lower production tubular right side valve is closed, upper production tubular is plumbed with t-shaped tubular and closed valve union, and the production tubular plumbed on left side (opposite meter) of head to sales/surface equipment with open valve; annulus is exposed and vented to the atmosphere with plumbed tubular sticking out of ground and open valve union (photos #3, #4, and #5). Meter reading (photo #6). No Well label/marker is affixed to wellhead. The wellhead is in close, visible proximity to the production facility and does not require a well label/marker. Some trace to occasionally moderate corrosion at the wellhead on the production/surface casing steel unions, lubricator, and tubulars. The surface/ground production facility, one 50 bbl poly tank, and one 100 bbl steel tank all contained by a shallow earthen dike (photo #5). Functioning pressure gauge atop separator unit in line recording ~40 psi at time of inspection (photo #6). Valve open on main tubular feeding separator and open valves to and from separator (photo #7). A 31-day production chart is present with recordings and dated 12/1/22 (photo #8). Well posting signage affixed to steel tank with all information about well and current Operator present, except the Operator contact address information (photo #9). Fair to occasionally moderate corrosion on ground production unit equipment and tank. Notice of violation (NOV) issued for Well posting OGA3211(G). Comments: On April 25, 2024, inspection conducted at the US Natural Resources 1-P085 well site in Somerset Township, Washington County. This inspection follows up to IR 3744557, which documents the Department's response to a spill that reportedly occurred on April 10, 2024, when the onsite brine tank overfilled with production fluid and pushed a grease-like layer sitting on top of this fluid out the top of the tank onto the ground below. Present at this inspection were KPI representative Joel Grecko and myself. Mr. Grecko reports that remediation of the impacted area was completed on April 16, 2024. The following was observed:The access road appeared to be stable at the time of inspection with no observed evidence of accelerated erosion or sedimentation (see photo 1). Tire rutting was observed in the well site at the time of inspection (see photo 2). The area impacted by the grease-like substance was excavated with no staining observed in this area (see photo 3). No elevated soil conductivity was detected in this area, underneath the brine tank valve, or within the majority of the earthen berm surrounding the brine tank (see photos 4, 6, 7, 8, and 9). An area of slightly elevated conductivity was detected in the southwestern corner of the earthen berm surrounding the brine tank (see photos 5 and 9). However, no staining, distressed vegetation, or other visual impacts were observed in this area. The well head was equipped with a well tag, and no staining or distressed vegetation was observed on the ground around it (see photos 10 and 11). The operator's information was posted on the meter box (see photo 13). The brine tank appeared to be sound at the time of inspection, with any remaining grease-like substances appearing to have wiped off (see photo 14). Mr. Grecko was conducting brush clearing onsite when the Department arrived. Based on observations from this inspection, the Department recommends that maintenance is conducted on the well site (and on the access road, if needed) now that remediation is complete to address the aforementioned tire rutting. The Department recommends that the operator assess and evaluate the area of elevated conductivity in the earthen berm, as the conductivity reading taken in this location is an outlier when compared to other soil conductivity readings taken onsite. Finally the Department recommends that the remediated area is mulched and seeded until 70 percent vegetative growth coverage is achieved. The Department requests a response to this inspection report from the operator with the waste manifest from remediation included in this response, when available.Violations shall be noted and immediately corrected.

Inspection Date: 4/09/2026
Comments: On 04/09/2026 the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow up inspection at Repsol's UGLIUZZA Well Pad in Pike Township, Bradford County. The weather was 42 degrees and sunny. Water Quality Specialist Korey Starkey and I arrived at 0930 hours. The DEP traveled the area of the impact beginning at the release point (CTS #396090) (photo #2). The DEP was unable to field measure the Electrical Conductivity (EC) at the release point due to stimulation activities. The EC of the fluids up-gradient of the stormwater basin were ~ 240 us/cm (photo #3). The stormwater basin with containment has one 24/7 water truck recovering fluids on top of and underneath the containment and from the sumps. The EC of the fluids on top of the containment were ~ 277 us/cm (photo #4). The EC of the fluids in the sump located down gradient of where overflow pipe was located were ~ 742 us/cm (photo #6). Temporary E and S controls have been installed down gradient of the stormwater basin (photo #6). The EC of the soil down gradient of the stormwater basin was ~4.0 mS/cm. On 04/03/2026 an additional sump was installed further down gradient (photo #9). The additional sump is manned 24/7. Fluids are recovered from the sump ~ every hour. The EC of the fluids in the additional sump were ~1.4 mS/cm (1400 us/cm) (photo #10). The EC of fluids down gradient of the additional sump were between 101-104 us/cm. At the 03/25/2026 sample location (0983-529) UNT to Rockwell Creek upstream of the discharge the EC of the fluids were 71 us/cm (photo #13). The EC of the fluids entering UNT to Rockwell Creek upstream of the confluence were ~ 935 us/cm (photo #14). At the 03/25/2026 sample location (0983-530) from UNT Rockwell Creek downstream of the discharge the EC of fluids were ~160 us/cm. As of 04/06/2026 5,293 barrels (166,729 gallons) have been recovered onsite. Resource management will continue screening and sampling ten monitoring points twice a week. Fluids on the pad surface were field measured for EC between 430-640 us/cm. There was no evidence of any additional spills or releases. Proper secondary containment was observed throughout the site. Stimulation activities are to be continued until 04/30/2026.Violations remain open against API #015-23994. We departed at 1115 hours.

The EC of the fluids on top of the containment were ~ 277 us/cm (photo #4). The EC of the fluids in the sump located down gradient of where overflow pipe was located were ~ 742 us/cm (photo #6). Temporary E and S controls have been installed down gradient of the stormwater basin (photo #6). The EC of the soil down gradient of the stormwater basin was ~4.0 mS/cm. On 04/03/2026 an additional sump was installed further down gradient (photo #9). The additional sump is manned 24/7. Fluids are recovered from the sump ~ every hour. The EC of the fluids in the additional sump were ~1.4 mS/cm (1400 us/cm) (photo #10). The EC of fluids down gradient of the additional sump were between 101-104 us/cm. Fluids on the pad surface were field measured for EC between 430-640 us/cm. There was no evidence of any additional spills or releases. Proper secondary containment was observed throughout the site. Stimulation activities are to be continued until 04/30/2026.Violations remain open against API #015-23994. We departed at 1115 hours.

Comments: On December 15, 2023, I conducted an inspection of the WL Hopkins Well Site. The inspection was conducted in response to a request made by an PA DEP OGI during an inspection conducted on 12/15/2023 (Sub-SAIR# 3660126). At the time of inspection, the following was observed:Act 9 Sign Installed, however the Operator of Record does not appear to be correct. The associated PPC plan and ER plan on site have not been updated to reflect the change in ownership. (Photo 11 and 12)The COASTAL Drill Rig was on site and connected to the well. The drill rig and associated equipment was not placed within secondary containment. (Photo 1)I observed fluid on the well pad surrounding the WL Hopkins 590312 Well and drill rig. I also observed fluid within the well cellar. I collected conductivity readings of the fluid on the well pad and within the cellar, which result in elevated conductivity readings. I also observed what appeared to be a light colored crystallin substance deposited on the well pad rock adjacent to the standing fluid. The crystallin substance appears to be salt which suggest that the fluid has been on site long enough to begin evaporation. The amount of fluid on the well pad appeared to be greater than 42 gallons. At the time of inspection, the Department was not previously notified by the Operator of a release of fluid to the well pad. (Photo 2 thru 10)While I was on site, I contacted Operator representative Kevin Wright (CONSOL/Leatherwood) to relay my observations related to the fluid release and recommend that the Operator being remediation immediately. Mr. Wright indicated that the Operator added brine to the well to kill the well on 11/15/2023.I am requesting clarification of the activity, date and time of when the fluid was added to the well bore and all information/inspections related to the monitoring of the well between 11/15/2023 and 12/15/2023. I am also requesting clarification of the source of the fluid added to the well bore on or around 11/15/2023.Violation are being issued for the release (78a.54, 78a57(a), 91.34(a), SWMA 301, 78a66(b)1,78a(b)1(i), 78a66(b)1(ii), 78a66(b)(2), 91.33(a) and 91.33(b).Violations are being issued for the failure to develop a site specific PPC plan and ER Plan. 78a55(a), 78a55(b), 78a55(c). 78a55(h).Violations are being issued for the failure to properly update the Act 9 Sign (78a55(i)(4)(D)(III).Violations are being issued for the failure to install secondary containment. (78a64(a))

properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to TURM OIL INC in Cherryhill Twp, Indiana County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 6/02/2022 to TURM OIL INC in Cherryhill Twp, Indiana county. 78.66(a) - REPORTING RELEASES - Owner or operator failed to comply with the reporting and corrective action requirements of 25 Pa. Code Section 91.33 when a release of a substance caused or threatened pollution to the Waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: TURM OIL INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/02/2022
Violation Code: 78.66(a) - REPORTING RELEASES - Owner or operator failed to comply with the reporting and corrective action requirements of 25 Pa. Code Section 91.33 when a release of a substance caused or threatened pollution to the Waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 957714
Permit API: 063-34032
Unconventional: No
County: Indiana
Municipality: Cherryhill Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/02/2022
Comments: On 6/2/22 at 0900 hrs., I conducted an inspection of Turm Oil, Inc.'s Paul Strong 4 well (API 063-34032) in Cherryhill Twp., Indiana Co. Mr. Bill Davis with Turm Oil was also present during the inspection. The inspection was conducted in response to a complaint, received by the Department on 6/1/22, of oil and produced water being released from a production fluids tank that was being removed from the site.I spoke with the complainant, the operator, and Mr. Davis on 6/1/22. The operator informed me that the well was sold to Rosebud Mining back in March; however there is no record of a well transfer filed with the Department. During our phone call, Mr. Davis informed me that the tank removal and release occurred around 1100 hrs. on 5/31/22. He estimated that approximately 10 gallons of crude oil and production fluid was released when removing the tank, and stated that some absorbent material was placed near the well and was subsequently containerized. Mr. Davis also acknowledged that some released fluid was covered up during regrading of the site.Upon inspection of the site, oil stained soil and vegetation was observed, beginning at the regraded area of the well pad, and continuing along a drainage ditch adjacent to the pad. There was a strong crude oil odor present. The impacted water in the ditch flowed to a nearby ephemeral stream where a slight sheen was observed. The black plastic bag containing the absorbent material Mr. Davis previously applied was located at the base of the well head; however, no additional measures were taken to prevent the material from reaching Waters of the Commonwealth. I advised Mr. Davis to place absorbent boom or pads to prevent further downstream impacts. I also advised Mr. Davis that regulations require removal of the pollutant from the soil and water within 15 days. In addition, I requested that Mr. Davis reinstall a well tag with the permit number on the well head.The release was not reported to the Department. Violations of 91.33(A), 78.66(a), 91.34(A), 78.66(b), and78.66(e) are cited and will be immediately closed as 'unresolvable'.Violations of CSL 301, CSL 307(a), CSL 402(b), 78.54, 78.57(a), SWMA 301, SWMA 302(a), and SWMA 610(1) are being cited for the release of crude oil and production fluid onto the ground and into Waters of the Commonwealth. These violations will be resolved upon remediation and temporary stabilization of the site, and submission of waste manifests for the disposal of impacted material to the Department.

Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection at Seneca Resources' Delaney J 651 well site located in Sullivan Township, Tioga County on 8/28/2025 at 0930 hours. The weather was 63 degrees F with partly cloudy skies. The inspection was conducted in response to a release reported by the operator. Complaints Tracking System (CTS) ID# 391708 is tied to this release within CTS.Seneca Resources notified the DEP via the reporting hotline that on 8/25/2025 at 1400 hours a plunger system cracked on the well pad releasing 15 to 20 gallons of produced water to the gravel pad surface. Seneca Resources dispatched a team to screen impacted pad material and recover as necessary. Seneca provided me with photos of the release area before and after remediation. The impacted area, prior to remediation, can be seen in photos #6-8. The area excavated, prior to backfilling, can be seen in photos #1-4. Seneca conducted the remedial activities on 8/26 and 8/27. Impacted materials were placed in a lined, covered residual waste container, which is now stored in the corner of the well pad (photo #5). During my inspection, pad materials within the excavated area were field measured utilizing a Hanna Groline soil conductivity meter. All readings within the excavated area returned readings below 1.0mS/cm. No pooled fluids were observed within the excavated areas. Various pooled fluids in other areas on the pad surface were field measured and returned readings below 1.0mS/cm.Based on the reported release of produced fluids to the pad surface and the operators timely remedial response, violations of the following are cited as immediately corrected against API #117-21765:25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a), Clean Streams Law 402(b), Solid Waste Management Act 301I departed the site at 1100 hours.

No loose sediment was observed in the cross-culvert during this inspection. However, the Department recommended in IR 4186065 that the operator take necessary measures to ensure that the cross-culvert is protected from sedimentation.Based on observations from this inspection, violations issued in IR 4186065 shall remain outstanding. Additional violations shall be issued for failure to adequately protect the cross-culvert shown in Photo 14 and for failure maintain the RCE adjacent to the well plugging site. Additional volations may be forthcoming against the swirly rainbow sheen released adjacent to the well plugging rig.

Report Details

Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8215509
Permit API: 081-20563
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Cogan House Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 1/29/2025
Comments: On January 29, 2025, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an incident inspection at the EQT ARO LLC H Lyle Landon Well Pad A. This inspection is a follow up to EQT reporting a spill on January 24, 2025, where a dump to one of the production fluid tanks failed. Upon failing, the pressure caused production fluid to mist outside of containment onto the well pad surface. According to EQT, it was thought that the majority of the production fluid was released into the production fluid containment. DEP placed a phone call to Rick Hall with EQT at 0848 on January 29, 2025 to gather more information on the spill. Mr. Hall informed DEP that during EQT's investigation of the spill that more than a mist event had occurred. While the majority of the produced fluid spilled into containment, an area of high soil conductivity was found outside of containment to the south next to the containment wall. EQT suspects there is an area of the liner for the containment that is leaking. Since January 24, 2025, EQT has vacuumed all the fluid out of the containment and power washed the containment liner. Mr. Hall said there were no visible or apparent holes found. The impacted soil that could be removed has been excavated. EQT plans to remove the production fluid tanks and the containment to investigate and remove the remainder of the impacted soil underneath the containment. A schedule for this process has not yet been made. EQT plans to monitor the area and remove impacted soil or production fluid as needed until the area can be completely remediated. On January 24, 2025, Penn E and R was onsite to collect waste classification samples and oversee the excavation. EQT plans to go through the Act 2 remediation process due to the unknown volume of fluid that leaked through the containment.Due to the spill of production fluid outside of containment violations of Clean Streams Law 402(b), Chapter 78a.57(a), and Solid Waste Management Act 301 were noted.

Comments: On 08/06/2024 a routine complete inspection was conducted at the R STOPKO 5 OG Well in West Bethlehem Township, Washington County.The following was observed during inspection:-I observed deep accelerated erosion rills on the access road. It appears that sediment and gravel is washing off of the access road and onto Highland Ridge Road and into the road side ditch. Gravel is building up in the ditch. The department recommends maintenance to the access road and removal of gravel built up (Photo 1-9).- A well tag was observed on the well head (Photo 10).-The well and operator's information was displayed and visible at the well site as required by OGA 3211(g) (Photo 11).-Some corrosion was observed on the well, production equipment, and production tank (Photos 12-14). -I observed a fluid leaking along the production tank from the open pipe above. It appears that the pipe was disconnected and not capped. The pipe coming out of the ground appears to have fluid surrounding it, but it is capped. I recommend capping the open pipe to prevent further fluid leaking from it and cleaning the tank (Photo 15 and 16). Violations were issued for 78.53, 102.4(b)1, 102.11(a)1

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 7/24/2025 to TITUS ENERGY LLC in Monroe Township, Clarion county. 78.73(f) - GENERAL PROVISION FOR WELL CONSTRUCTION AND OPERATION - Operator failed to equip well with a check valve to prevent backflow from the pipelines into the well.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: TITUS ENERGY LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 7/24/2025
Violation Code: 78.73(f) - GENERAL PROVISION FOR WELL CONSTRUCTION AND OPERATION - Operator failed to equip well with a check valve to prevent backflow from the pipelines into the well.
Violation ID: 8241981
Permit API: 031-23676
Unconventional: No
County: Clarion
Municipality: Monroe Township
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 7/24/2025
Comments: This inspection was conducted as a follow up to Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection inspection #3978563 conducted on May 15 2025 at 0848. During the inspection, the wellhead and casing strings were visually assessed for signs of leakage, structural deterioration, or failure. While onsite the well appeared to be producing off of the 4" production string. The 7" intermediate casing was being vented to atmosphere through the annulus vent valve at a concentration of 94% combustible gas. To evaluate the potential for subsurface gas migration, four slam bar holes were installed approximately 6 inches to 1 foot from the well-bore in the cardinal directions. Each hole was placed to a depth of approximately 3 feet. Soil gas measurements were obtained using a Bascom-Turner Gas Explorer II meter, calibrated on July 24, 2025. The results were as follows: South and East slam bar holes: Non-detect for combustible gas. North slam bar hole: Peak reading of 3% LEL combustible gas; sustained reading of 1% LEL combustible gas. West slam bar hole: Peaking reading of 18% LEL combustible gas; sustained reading of 1% LEL combustible gas. Due to the lack of adequate sustained concentration, a viable sample for isotopic analysis could not be collected. On May 22, 2025 the Department received an email from the operator stating that "Titus would prefer to have the Johnson #1 well plugged". As of the completion of this inspection, the operator has not plugged the well nor remedied any of the outstanding violations associated with it. The Department requests a detailed timeline specifying when the well will be properly plugged or when corrective measures will be undertaken to bring the well into full regulatory compliance.
